_doc: Workspace topology. Turns an absolute path (seen only in memory, never stored) into a repo name and a coarse surface label. This is the one file worth editing on day one: point `code_roots` at wherever you actually keep repos. See docs/specs/Surface-Attribution.md.
_code_roots_doc: Where your repositories live. Longest match wins, so a nested root can override a broader one. `~` is expanded. Paths that match nothing are reported as unattributed rather than guessed at — a wrong attribution is worse than an honest gap.
_worktree_doc: Folder name under which git worktrees are kept, if you use them. A path inside one is attributed to the parent repository rather than to the worktree directory.
_special_roots_doc: Folders that are not repositories but are worth naming, so that time spent configuring your tooling shows up as exactly that instead of as unattributed noise.
_incidental_doc: Infrastructure, not a subject of work. A turn that only wrote a scratch file or opened a config folder is attributed to whatever real repo the session was actually about. These still stand on their own when a session touched nothing else.
_surface_rules_doc: Per repo, first matching glob wins. '*' matches one segment. '{n}' in the label is replaced by segment n of the matched path (0-based). Repo '*' rules apply to every repo, after that repo's own rules. Unmatched paths fall back to their first path segment, or '(root)' for a top-level file. A rule may only ever name a DIRECTORY — a rule that would interpolate the filename is skipped, so a document title can never become a permanent bucket (ADR-008).
_lanes_doc: Which usage lane a turn belongs to. Transcripts carry no account identity, so a lane is inferred from where and how the work happened. First matching rule wins; anything unmatched gets `default`. Keys usable in a rule: repo, entrypoint, provider. Set this up if you want work and side-project usage separated — most people want that separation and no vendor dashboard offers it.
